title: Summarising Your AI Agent's Chat History Can Triple Your Bill #shorts
caption:
Summarising your agent's chat history to save money can triple your bill. Here's the arithmetic.

The API is stateless. The model remembers nothing between calls, so you resend the whole conversation every turn. 20 turns of 1k tokens isn't 20k sent — it's 210k. A triangle.

The only reason that doesn't bankrupt you: most of it is identical to last time, so it comes back from cache at about a tenth of the price. Your bill isn't the length of the conversation. It's how much of it you're recomputing.

So you keep a running summary to keep the history small. And that's the trap — because the summary changes every turn. Different text, different prefix, and a different prefix is a cache miss. Those tokens were a tenth of the price; now they're more than full price, on every single request.

It's not compression that costs you. It's re-compression. Half the tokens, three times the bill.

The fix isn't compressing less — it's compressing less often:
① append only. Never edit the left-hand side of the prompt.
② order it never-changes-first: tools, system, docs, history, new message. Breakpoint on the last block that doesn't move.
③ when the window fills, compact ONCE and let that become the new prefix.

Same technique, opposite economics. The variable is frequency.

Two honest caveats: this assumes you're using prompt caching (if you're not, that's fix number one). And the 0.1x / 1.25x numbers are Anthropic's — the shape holds on any provider with prefix caching, the ratio doesn't.

Full arithmetic, script and canvas in the open vault — link in bio. Part 12. Follow along for the series.
